principle: Leon should keep working on local, reversible, in-scope project work without asking for approval every time.
may_continue_without_user_approval: editing project docs and source files in /home/per/leon-ai-assistant
creating local SQLite control-plane rows for tasks, proposals, routing decisions and audit events
running local tests, compile checks and read-only diagnostics
starting or restarting the local Leon dashboard process
creating reviewable plans, task proposals and local_mock agent runs
making reversible UI/dashboard improvements that do not expose secrets or external systems
must_request_user_approval: spending money or creating financial commitments
buying, bidding, paying, trading or moving funds
connecting personal accounts or OAuth providers
sending email/messages, posting publicly, or writing calendar events to external accounts
installing system packages, drivers, Docker services or third-party repos outside an approved sandbox
large downloads, model downloads, GPU-heavy jobs or actions likely to consume significant storage, VRAM, power or quota
server/container/firewall/DNS changes outside the local Leon dashboard process
destructive filesystem actions outside narrow project-local generated cache cleanup
exposing services publicly outside Tailscale tailnet
reading, printing or sending raw secret values
must_refuse_or_redirect: malware, phishing, spam or abusive automation
captcha bypass, anti-bot evasion or aggressive scraping
broad destructive commands against home, root, system or user data
notes: Approval is not required for normal Codex implementation work in the Leon project.
A preview plus explicit user confirmation is still required for external irreversible actions.
When uncertain, create a proposal/task and continue with safe local work instead of stopping the whole project.
